thread:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in DSAR deletion failures after last night's key maintenance. A subset of erasures are failing with KMS decrypt errors and are stuck in the erasure queue. Can infra/security take a look?

raj_infra: I pulled the erasure-processor logs. Sample error: `DECRYPT_FAILED: cryptoKeyVersion not found` for some snapshots. My working theory: IAM binding for the `dsar-eraser` service account didn't include the new key version after rotation.

elena_sec: That matches what I saw. We rotated the cryptoKey and updated aliases but forgot to add the SA to the new key's IAM policy in eu-west1.

tomas_sre: Triage checklist I'm running now:
- enumerate failed erase jobs (small sample)
- confirm KMS key versions referenced by ciphertexts
- verify SA permissions and recent IAM diffs

raj_infra: Log snippet for reference:
```
2026-03-21T02:14:22Z eraser-processor [job=erase-345] ERROR: DECRYPT_FAILED: cryptoKeyVersion not found projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/kr-01/cryptoKeys/ks-prod/cryptoKeyVersions/3
```

mina_ops: Short-term unblock option: grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` to `dsar-eraser@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` scoped to the new key for 1 hour, run a targeted backfill for the failed list, then revoke. This requires a retention-exception / emergency breakglass record for audit.

olivia_legal: Legal will need a clear audit trail if anyone touches the data. If you do a temporary grant, record the who/why/start-end times and attach approvals to the ticket. No data exports allowed.

elena_sec: Proposed controlled plan:
- Create a timebound IAM binding (1 hour) granting decrypt on the new key version to `dsar-eraser` only.
- Run a throttled backfill for the failed job list (no re-encryption, only decrypt->verify->erase).
- Record everything in an incident ticket + retention-exception stub and set forensic audit flag.
- Remove binding and confirm no new ciphertexts were created; rotate aliases as needed.

maya: Important Q: will the backfill re-encrypt or only decrypt existing ciphertexts? We must avoid creating any new ciphertexts.

raj_infra: Backfill logic: decrypt -> validate -> mark erased. It does not re-encrypt. So granting decrypt should allow stalled jobs to complete.

privacy-bot: Automated note: DSAR operations that modify keystore permissions require `forensic_audit` flag set on the ticket. Attach `evidence-proof` after completion.

mina_ops: I'll open a retention-exception ticket with scope = list of snapshot IDs, justification = remediate failed erasures after key rotation, duration = 1 hour, approvers = sec lead + legal, mitigation = no export + live audit.

olivia_legal: I can provisionally approve subject to sec lead verification and signed entry in the ticket.

elena_sec: Before any permission change: paste the affected snapshot IDs and the exact KMS resource name here so I can verify minimal scope and review the IAM diff.

maya: Affected snapshots (sample): snapshot-20260318-9a3c, snapshot-20260319-1f7d, snapshot-20260320-ebb2. KMS resource: projects/redwood/locations/eu/keyRings/kr-01/cryptoKeys/ks-prod (alias now points v4).

raj_infra: IAM change snippet (example) — we will timebox and schedule removal:
```
# grant decrypt for exactly 1 hour
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ks-prod \
  --location=eu --keyring=kr-01 \
  --member=serviceAccount:dsar-eraser@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
# plan: run backfill, then revoke with scheduled job or manual revoke
```

mina_ops: Ticket created: REQ-20260321-01 https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/REQ-20260321-01 — added scope, approvers, and retention-exception template with `audit_artifact` placeholder.

elena_sec: I reviewed the IAM diff and scope. Approving the timebound grant with the condition that we watch logs in real time. If we see any sign of data exfiltration we abort and revoke immediately.

tomas_sre: I'll limit backfill concurrency to 5 qps to avoid overloading workers and to keep logs readable.

maya: Action owners: raj applies the timebound binding and runs the backfill, mina owns the retention-exception ticket, elena audits live and signs off, olivia posts legal sign-off in the ticket.

raj_infra: Starting in 15m. Will post gcloud outputs and backfill progress to the ticket and paste stdout for failed→succeeded job IDs.

mina_ops: Added the approval checklist and `forensic_audit` flag in REQ-20260321-01. Linking logs and approver signatures.

olivia_legal: Legal sign-off posted in the ticket with required fields.

elena_sec: Verified the audit logs during the window. No export attempts observed. Confirmed backfill completed for the sample items. Revoking binding now.

raj_infra: Backfill complete for the sample list: snapshot-20260318-9a3c (erased), snapshot-20260319-1f7d (erased), snapshot-20260320-ebb2 (erased). Removing the temporary IAM binding.

mina_ops: Closing retention-exception REQ-20260321-01. Attached `evidence-proof` artifacts and command output.

maya: Thanks everyone. Reopening if any other failures surface. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
